When you have multiple points of interest on your chart, do not automatically choose the cleanest order block or the nearest fair value gap.

Use this checklist to filter them properly👇:

1. Establish the context📈

☐ What is my higher-timeframe bias?
☐ What is the current dealing range?
☐ For a buy, is my point of interest in discount?
☐ For a sell, is my point of interest in premium?

2. Identify the available PD arrays🔍

☐ Order block
☐ Reclaimed block
☐ Mitigation block
☐ Fair value gap
☐ Swing high or swing low
☐ Breaker block

3. Eliminate the weaker points of interest

☐ Does it align with the higher-timeframe narrative?
☐ Is it positioned correctly within the dealing range?
☐ Did it contribute to a structural break or shift?
☐ Is there a clear liquidity reason for price to reach it?
☐ Has the area already been significantly mitigated?
☐ Where does it rank within the PD-array hierarchy explained in the video?

4. Validate the entry✅

☐ Has my required entry confirmation appeared?
☐ Do I know exactly where the trade becomes invalid?
☐ Does the setup offer an acceptable risk-to-reward ratio?
☐ Have I defined my monetary risk before entering?

The goal is not to find the prettiest zone on the chart. The goal is to identify the point of interest that makes the most sense within the complete market narrative.

If two same POI still appear equally valid, you do not have to guess. Allow price action to provide more confirmation.

You're 7% in drawdown on your prop firm evaluation.

Your maximum drawdown is 10%.

What do you do?

a) Full-port the next trade.
b) Keep everything exactly the same.
c) Lower your risk.

Trade the model, not the PnL.

If you’re only trading to chase profits or pass your prop firm challenge asap, you’ll burn out.

You’ll be emotionally attached to every trade, and every loss will hit you like a hammer.

That mindset, that approach, it’ll mentally drain you.

Instead, find a model/strategy that suits you, learn the model, gain experience with it, and execute mechanically with confidence.

The motivation should be to execute the model in the best and highest quality way possible, not to make the most money in a short time period.

If you manage to rewire your brain into this, the money will naturally follow.

🤖@agenticscredit put real numbers behind the pitch. The ACS runs 300 to 850, same range as a traditional credit score, and 580 is the line where trading credit opens up.

Below it you paper trade to build a record. Above it you get a funded account with position and leverage ceilings.

The detail that matters: real money is weighted heaviest. A clean sim week can't paper over poor live performance, and if your blended score drops too far, every credit line pauses at once.

Borrowing the exact shape of consumer credit and pointing it at agents is a sharper idea than most things flying around this space.
